analysis: The closest option combines media interpretation and production with Python, R data work, databases, machine learning, sociology and ethics. The technical courses give a sustained computational toolkit, while the media and communication courses provide objects and questions for inquiry. General algorithms and AI are useful supporting tools but do not substitute for digital-media methods.

The second option shares technical foundations and gives distinct depth in museum and heritage interpretation, art and literature, historical inquiry and film adaptation. Databases and data analysis support the organisation and examination of cultural evidence, but UCR does not offer a dedicated archives and digital humanities lab sequence.

The third option combines film, environmental media, race and representation, documentary, stylistics, public rhetoric and social and behavioural research. From T.V. to TikTok adds direct study of representation across television, film and contemporary digital forms. Communicating the Climate Crisis adds discourse across texts, films, protest art and social media. The business gateway supports Strategy & Digital Transformation, which stays as an organisational application. General leadership, market research and conflict were displaced. The option supports study of mediated public life without claiming platform engineering or data journalism.

Replaced generic closest-counterpart formulas with a small set of supported overlaps in Python, empirical data methods, media change, media analysis and research design. Institutional archive, lab and thesis components remain separate. All three schedules pass current feasibility and distinctness rules.

alignment.rationale: Both develop programming in Python. UCR teaches general computational problem-solving, while UvA applies code to cultural objects and data.
Both collect and analyse digital data. UCR teaches a general R workflow. UvA applies digital methods to media and information research.
Both use concepts to analyse media forms and practices. UCR emphasises film form and media history.
Both examine how media technologies change and shape cultural practice. UCR uses historical objects and infrastructures.
Both develop research design and qualitative interpretation. UCR uses interviews, ethnography and other social-science methods. UvA applies research to media cases.
